name: OmniQuant: Omnidirectionally Calibrated Quantization for Large Language Models
authors: Shi, Zhang, Yang, Wang, Meng, Wang
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong / University of Sydney
problem: PTQ methods hand-craft their quantization parameters (clipping thresholds, equivalent transformations), which is why they degrade at INT3/INT4-W4A4.
mechanism: Block-wise error-minimization framework that learns the quantization parameters rather than hand-designing them, via two components: Learnable Weight Clipping (LWC) optimizes the weight clipping threshold to reshape extreme values; Learnable Equivalent Transformation (LET) shifts activation outliers into the weights by learning a per-channel scale folded into the preceding LayerNorm, so the activation-side quantization difficulty is moved to the weight side. Trained per block on 128 calibration samples, then the block is frozen.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): LLaMA-2 7B-70B processed on a SINGLE A100-40G within 1-16 h per model (this is a calibration-cost claim, not a speedup); 'good performance in diverse quantization settings while maintaining the computational efficiency of PTQ'. COMPRESSION RATIO: covers weight-only and W4A4/W4A8 settings, i.e. up to ~4x on weights and up to 8x combined for W4A8. QUALITY COST: the abstract gives no paired perplexity delta - it points at per-setting tables. speedup_reported here is therefore the calibration-cost figure, which is what the abstract actually quantifies.
